examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'water' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vanya, the water! There's water everywhere!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'meeting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('see you') (in 'до встречи' = until we meet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'man'.
Secondary conversational sense ('real man, tough guy') (как мужик = like a real man) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You should have acted like a real man!

examples.text: Что мы, мы? Тебе надо было как мужик!
examples.trans: What do you mean, we? You should have acted like a man!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец').

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.

неважно.gloss: it does not matter, never mind, poorly

meanings.en: it does not matter, never mind
meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'важно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: That completely does not matter right now.
Never mind, let us forget about it.
Never mind, pour me some water quickly.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'nervous' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Работа на кухне очень трудная и нервная.
examples.trans: Work in the kitchen is very hard and nerve-wracking.

Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'full' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('complete, total, utter') (полный кошмар = a total nightmare) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!

пронести.gloss: to carry past; to blow over, to dodge trouble

meanings.en: to carry past; to blow over (trouble passed)
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'нести'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to carry past', forming an aspectual pair with 'проносить'.

examples.text: Слава богу, на этот раз пронесло.
examples.trans: Thank goodness, this time trouble blew over.
The danger passed by, disaster was averted.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.
